language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I’m Paolo. I work part-time at a pizzeria. I am also interested in do-it-yourself science as a hobby. I keep a little tool box with me because I love to fix things when I’m not busy.
My latest hobby is making magnets. You have probably played with magnets before, like those on a refrigerator.
Wouldn't it be cool if you could actually make one? Believe me, magnets are quite easy to make. Let me show you what I was able to do right here at the restaurant.
Paolo is clever at using simple objects for his science experiments. Let’s see what he’s up to today.

I’ve been waiting to try this Do-It-Yourself kit to make an electromagnet. I have the instructions here, but I could use your help. Why don't you look at the pictures on the instructions and tell me what to do?

Wait, do you know what an electromagnet is? It's really cool. It's like a magnet, but it only works when it's powered by electricity. If you turn the power off, the magnet stops working. Then, when you power it on again, it's magnetic again. Come on, let's build one together!

helperSimple.text: Paolo wants to know what to do with each item in the D-I-Y kit to make an electromagnet. Select the right answer for each part in the kit.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What do I need to do with the battery to make an electromagnet?

answers.text: Tap the nail's tip on the positive battery terminal.
Wind the insulated wire around the battery.
Connect each end of the wire with one side of the battery.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What do I need to do with the cutter to make an electromagnet?

answers.text: Bend the nail into a U-shape.
Strip the insulation from the ends of the wire.
Hold one end of the wire as you wrap it tightly around the battery.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What do I need to do with the insulated wire to make an electromagnet?

answers.text: Wrap the wire tightly around the nail.
Wrap the wire tightly around the battery.
Cut the wire into one-inch strips.

outro.text: Thank you for helping me figure out what each part is used for. Now it should be easy to build an electromagnet.

I want to show my friend Peter how to build a compass magnet. That is a magnet that always points north. He thinks its a bit hard, so I was wondering if you could help him. Would you? Great, thanks!
OK, here is how it works: I've got a magnet, a steel pin, a cork, and a bowl of water. There are only three steps to make a compass magnet. I've put them on a list.
Step 1 is rubbing the pin quickly over the magnet. The pin is now magnetic.
For step 2 you place the magnetic pin on the cork.
For step 3 you place the cork with the pin on top in the bowl of water and tadaa! The pin will point north.
Now, you can help Peter by selecting the correct steps?

activities.title: Which image represents this step? Click on it.
activities.subtitle: STEP 1: Rub the metal piece repeatedly against the magnet.

activities.title: Which image represents this step? Click on it.
activities.subtitle: STEP 2: Place magnetized steel pin on cork.

activities.title: Which image represents this step? Click on it.
activities.subtitle: STEP 3: Float the cork with the pin in a bowl of water.

outro.text: Well, wasn't it easy to build a compass magnet? Thank you for helping Peter and me.
